chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi and Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who is muqatib (a slave who has agreed to pay a certain sum for his freedom) who dies having paid part of his manumission contract, and he has a son from his concubine: He said, 'If it was stipulated that if he became unable [to pay], he would remain a slave, then his son returns as a slave along with the concubine. And if it was not stipulated, then his son pays what remains of the manumission contract and inherits what remains [of the estate].'

key_terms.جَارِيَتِهِ: His concubine (female slave with whom he has relations)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract to pay a specific sum to his master in exchange for freedom
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission contract or the agreed-upon payment for freedom

ai.seo_question: What happens to the son and estate of a slave who dies while paying off his manumission contract?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a muqatib's offspring and estate based on the specific contractual stipulation (shart) regarding partial payment failure. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the default assumption is freedom and inheritance unless a specific condition of re-enslavement was explicitly agreed upon, reflecting the flexibility of mukataba contracts in Fiqh al-Ja'fari. The hadith underscores the importance of contractual precision in determining whether the son assumes the remaining debt or inherits the residual assets.
